commands.name: init
commands.summary: set up a node on this machine from nothing: a repository root, a credential at 0600, an actor key the node will trust, and a .choir/config so the other commands stop asking which node you mean; refuses and names what exists rather than overwriting a token nothing can reissue

commands.name: key
commands.summary: mint a key and print the line the operator registers; pass your channel name to print the bound form

commands.name: git-credential
commands.summary: git credential helper: hands git your token on stdin so it never lives in a remote URL; configure once with `git config credential.helper '''!choir git-credential <auth-file>'''`

commands.name: join
commands.summary: redeem an operator's invite and mint your actor key in one step; --user names the account, which most invites leave for you to pick and which the op log then keeps forever; writes the issued token to an auth file at 0600, and on a node started with --invite-binds-keys the key is registered by the redemption itself

commands.name: invite
commands.summary: mint an invite and print the one link to send; the same thing the node's /people page does, for when a terminal is where you are

commands.name: asks
commands.summary: who has asked for access and is waiting on an answer (D72)

commands.name: grant
commands.summary: let one of them in; the link they already hold becomes their invite, so there is nothing to send

commands.name: decline
commands.summary: drop a pending request; their link then reads as one that was never valid

commands.name: workspace
commands.summary: provision a CoW workspace; advanced flags owner-sign an exact base and stable change, and each --path owner-signs a subtree this change declares it works within

commands.name: checkpoint
commands.summary: publish an immutable change revision after committing and pushing its Git object

commands.name: propose
commands.summary: create a change, push its commits and request review; run it from a git checkout, which is where the node and the repository come from, the revision is checkpointed on the way, and the branch name is the change identity, so re-running after an amend updates the same proposal

commands.name: workspace-archive
commands.summary: owner-sign and recoverably archive a bound workspace; exact retries are idempotent

commands.name: runner
commands.summary: drive one workspace lifecycle step for an orchestrator; a JSON request on stdin, a JSON result on stdout

commands.name: submit
commands.summary: sign and submit one raw operation

commands.name: schema
commands.summary: print this node's machine-readable API description and its live capabilities

commands.name: log
commands.summary: read log entries from a cursor; --verify checks continuity, recomputes every hash, and verifies the signatures whose keys you hold — SYNC.md as a flag

commands.name: batch
commands.summary: sign and submit many operations as one batch — the primary path for agent workloads; one op per line, `-` reads stdin, one result line per op in order

commands.name: review
commands.summary: request review on a commit; name no reviewers and the node draws them

commands.name: verdict
commands.summary: answer a review you were assigned

commands.name: comment
commands.summary: say something on a review; append-only and permanent, and the comment id is your retry identity

commands.name: viewed
commands.summary: record that you read a review, so its author can tell "reviewed and ignored" from "nobody looked"; first read only, resubmitting is refused

commands.name: witness
commands.summary: cosign the node's current ref-state attestation (D67); the snapshot id is read from the view rather than passed, so a witness cannot attest a ref-state it did not look at, and the node may not witness its own

commands.name: vouch
commands.summary: vouch for another operator; both ends need a key bound in the log, it authorizes nothing on its own, and there is no score

commands.name: unvouch
commands.summary: withdraw a vouch; the edge leaves the view and both ops stay in the log, so vouching again is allowed and starts a fresh clock

commands.name: slash
commands.summary: invalidate one reviewer's approval; operator-only and never moves a ref

commands.name: abandon
commands.summary: archive a stale incomplete review as lapsed, settling it unapproved; operator-only and never moves a ref

commands.name: bind
commands.summary: record in the log that a key belongs to an operator; operator-only and never moves a ref

commands.name: revoke
commands.summary: withdraw a key binding; terminal, and the attribution row survives

commands.name: appeal
commands.summary: appeal a rejected newcomer attempt for operator adjudication; never grants privilege

commands.name: intent
commands.summary: publish a task spec or plan so other agents can see intent

commands.name: check
commands.summary: report one automated check's outcome on a commit; any runner or a person can report by signing, and the node never runs the check

commands.name: checks
commands.summary: every check reported on a commit, and one verdict; exits 0 passed, 1 failed or unreported, 3 still running, 4 could not be run

commands.name: profile
commands.summary: what the log records about one actor: keys and their age, changes owned, verdicts given, checks reported

commands.name: search
commands.summary: find a term across every repository you may read; the term is literal, not a pattern

commands.name: reviews
commands.summary: your pending review queue

commands.name: acl render
commands.summary: rewrite an ACL file's trailing comments to name the person behind each handle; the grants themselves are copied through unchanged, and a handle the node can no longer name loses its comment

commands.name: triage
commands.summary: every review and change classified into a bucket — landed, awaiting verdicts, changes requested, approved awaiting landing — ranked most-actionable-first, capped, with truncation marked in-band

commands.name: funnel
commands.summary: the contribution funnel from admission to first verdict, and the steepest drop between two stages; counts what this credential may read, and reports the first-contact stage as null rather than inventing a zero

commands.name: state
commands.summary: list what you owe and what you are waiting on; bounded, and every row carries the command that answers it and that command's risk

commands.name: docs
commands.summary: build this repository's documentation: the book from `docs/`, and the API documentation inside it at `book/api/` so the prose can link to a type; needs a checkout and `mdbook`, and refuses with the command that installs it

commands.name: skill
commands.summary: install the choir agent skill (default .claude/skills), rendered from this binary's own surface table so it can never document another version; re-run after upgrading and unchanged files are left alone

commands.name: view
commands.summary: read the materialized view, its ref-state attestation and the node's health counters; map-shaped sections page 200 rows at a time, with `<section>_omitted` and `paging.next` describing the rest

commands.name: repo create
commands.summary: create a repository on a running node, hooked into the sequencer from its first push, without restarting anything; needs a node-wide write grant, answers 409 rather than an error when it already exists, and prints the clone URL because cloning is what happens next

commands.name: repo list
commands.summary: the repositories on a node this credential can read, one per line; an ACL narrows the list rather than refusing it, and the command says which of the two empty answers it is giving

commands.name: repo url
commands.summary: the clone URL for a repository, with the one line of git configuration that makes pushing to it work; the credential is never put in the URL, because a URL is pasted into shells, screenshots and issue trackers and a token in one is a token in all three

commands.name: node serve
commands.summary: run the node in this terminal, deriving its repository root, credential and trusted-key file from the layout `choir init` wrote, so starting one takes the same arguments as creating one — none; execs the daemon rather than wrapping it, so signals and the exit code reach the real process

commands.name: node install
commands.summary: hand the node to this machine's service manager — a launchd agent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux — so it survives a logout, a crash and a reboot; the unit runs `choir node serve`, so a flag changing later never means re-rendering it

commands.name: node stop
commands.summary: stop the supervised node for this boot, leaving the unit in place so it returns at next login; `node uninstall` is the one that ends it

commands.name: node restart
commands.summary: reload the unit and start it again, which is how a rebuilt binary reaches the running node; the unit is torn down and re-bootstrapped rather than kicked, because a kick relaunches the arguments the service manager cached rather than the ones on disk

commands.name: node uninstall
commands.summary: stop the node and remove its unit so it does not come back; the state directory is kept, because the keys, the repositories and the op log are in it and no command of ours deletes those

commands.name: node logs
commands.summary: the tail of the node's log, wherever this machine's service manager was told to write it; defaults to the last 30 lines

commands.name: node status
commands.summary: what the node is doing right now: health, the commit actually serving, the sequencer's position and its measured p99 against the 100 ms gate, and how much this credential can see; sections a narrower credential may not read say so rather than reading as an idle node

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: check everything the other commands assume: the binaries this workspace shells out to, the auth file and its mode, and whether a node answers; each failure prints the command that fixes it, and a missing optional tool warns rather than fails

commands.name: backup verify
commands.summary: whether a backup can be restored from, which is a different claim from whether one was written; checks the four files, the manifest checksum, the hash chain, the policy archive and every git bundle, and refuses a backup that carries a key or a credential — every check local, nothing asked of the node it is a copy of

commands.name: backup restore
commands.summary: turn a backup back into a node, and refuse to say it worked until the restored node has accepted a real push: it reads and refuses before it writes a byte, unbundles the git objects before the first boot, then rehearses on a port it picks itself and proves the append chained onto what it replayed; exit 3 means a secret only you can supply is missing

commands.name: repair
commands.summary: inspect a stopped node's op log, or repair a tail that was still being written; `--verify` walks the hash chain and changes nothing, `--truncate-tail` quarantines the partial record to a sidecar before cutting, and damage anywhere but the tail is refused rather than patched over

deprecations.name: workspace
deprecations.note: v1 alias for the signature-covered attribution channel; accepted on submission for compatibility, and refused when it disagrees with `channel` rather than one silently winning

endpoints.name: choir_submit
endpoints.purpose: Submit one signed operation (hex payload, hex signature)

ops.description: Signed operations, admitted in array order

endpoints.name: choir_submit_batch
endpoints.purpose: Same, in array order; the primary path for agent workloads (throughput figures live in the build log, not here, so they cannot go stale)

limit.description: Rows per section; defaults to 200 and clamps to this range

offset.description: Rows skipped per section, in key order

endpoints.name: choir_view
endpoints.purpose: The materialized view plus the latest ref-state attestation, durable key bindings, T2 new-actor review outcomes, T3 concentration, T4 newcomer harm, complete-view growth, the commit this daemon was built from, and the sequencer's measured decision latency against the 100 ms gate. On a node running an ACL you are served your own slice: the repositories your credential may read, plus reviews you were assigned to; the node-wide sections need a node-wide grant. A repository missing from the response is one you were not granted, not one that is gone. Every map-shaped section is bounded: `limit` rows each (200 by default, 1000 at most), `offset` rows skipped in key order, `<section>_omitted` counting what this page left out, and `paging.next` naming the request that fetches the rest or being null when there is none

attempt_id.description: Newcomer attempt id returned with the rejection

endpoints.name: choir_appeal
endpoints.purpose: Record an appeal for a rejected newcomer attempt; it requests operator adjudication and never changes privilege

endpoints.name: choir_log
endpoints.purpose: Ordered log entries, the catch-up and sync primitive. Absolute `from`: entries evicted from the in-memory window are served from the persisted log (`source` says which), and a node that cannot reach that far back answers 409 rather than a page with a hole in it. Each entry carries its hash, parent and author signature so pages can be chained and verified without trusting the node; SYNC.md is that procedure

base.description: Exact full Git commit oid; advanced requests provide this with owner, change and idempotency_key

owner.description: Registered signing channel allowed to checkpoint and archive the stable change

payload_hex.description: Hex-encoded CreateAuthorization for the exact binding

signature_hex.description: Owner signature over the create authorization

endpoints.name: choir_workspace
endpoints.purpose: Provision a CoW workspace; optional exact base/change binding makes retries idempotent

change.description: Stable logical change id returned by creation

channel.description: Bound change owner and signature-covered attribution channel

payload_hex.description: Hex-encoded ArchiveAuthorization naming this exact change, workspace and revision

endpoints.name: choir_workspace_archive
endpoints.purpose: Recoverably archive a change-bound workspace and remove it from the active view

limit.description: Rows per section; defaults to 200 and clamps to this range

offset.description: Rows skipped per section, in key order

endpoints.name: choir_reviews
endpoints.purpose: One actor's pending review queue

endpoints.name: choir_schema
endpoints.purpose: This surface, machine-readable and versioned, plus what this particular node will accept — the description an agent generates a client from (D17)

in.description: What to look through; defaults to code

limit.description: Matches returned; defaults to 200. `matches` counts everything found either way

q.description: Literal term, not a pattern; matching is case-insensitive

repo.description: One repository as owner/name; omit to search every repository you may read

rev.description: Revision to search, for a single repo= only; defaults to HEAD

endpoints.name: choir_search
endpoints.purpose: Search repository contents, file names or commit messages. Node-wide by default: every repository your credential may read, each at its own HEAD, which is why `rev` is accepted only alongside a single `repo`. A repository you were not granted is absent from the results and, asked for by name, is answered exactly as one that does not exist. Unindexed -- one `git grep` per repository -- so `limit` bounds what comes back while `matches` still counts everything found, and `truncated` says which happened. The same search the browser pages run, so the two cannot disagree about what a match is

channel.description: The name an actor signs as

endpoints.name: choir_profile
endpoints.purpose: One actor's standing, counted out of the view you may already see: the keys bound to them and how many ops ago, changes they own, reviews they were assigned and the verdicts they gave, approvals slashed, checks they reported. It is a reading of `/api/view` and never a wider one -- two callers with different grants get different numbers about the same actor, which is the point. `vouches` names the operator whose graph it is (a vouch is between operators, so `ops/agent` reads `ops`), who vouches for them and whether each edge points both ways. D24 wants key age, vouches, scoped grants and bonds for Sybil resistance; two of the four are reported here as inputs, because a score would be a weighting of one against the other that nobody has measured. Scoped grants exist since D66 and are absent from this reading on purpose: a time-locked grant lives in the node's authorization files rather than in the log, so nothing counted out of the view can see one
This surface, as text, for an agent that has never seen choir
The sync contract, in full: cursor semantics and how to verify a page's hash chain and author signatures without trusting the node serving them

Which repositories this credential can see, from the filesystem rather than the view — a repository is not an entity in the view, and `portable::repos` already answers which ones exist by walking the root. Narrowed rather than refused, like the other aggregate reads: `narrowed` says whether an ACL was applied, so "you can see none" is distinguishable from "there are none".

Create a repository on a running node, with the `pre-receive` hook that puts its pushes in the sequencer's order; needs a node-wide write grant, because there is no repository yet to be scoped to. Nothing is appended to the log: a repository is not a value in the view, and which ones exist is answered by the filesystem, as the export already does
Where the op log and the bare repos disagree about a ref, read-only

Mint a single-use, expiring invite for a new account and the grants it will hold; needs a node-wide write grant, and can never issue one. A grant may carry its own deadline, `owner/repo write until=<unix seconds>` (D66); the invite's expiry bounds redemption, never what redemption hands over
Redeem an invite — presented as the credential — for a token, once, and register an ssh key with it
Answer somebody who asked for access (D72): turns their pending request into an invite under the id and secret they already hold, so the link they were given starts working with nothing sent
Drop a pending access request. Their link then says only that it is not valid, the same as a link that never existed
Delete an account: its token stops authenticating on the next request, and its grants and keys go with it
Who holds an account, what they were granted, and which invites are outstanding; never a secret or its hash
Internal: the pre-receive hook callback
Internal: retracts a refused push's already-accepted refs
